# SK9007 — `skala.jsonc` is not valid JSON

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala.jsonc` did not parse, so no tool configuration was read: the canonical drift policy fell back to `error` and the `exclude` list to empty. The message quotes the parser's own line and position. `skala config check` fails on it without `--strict`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tool |
| Default severity | error |
| Scope | Compilation |
| Needs a compilation | no |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 0.1 |

## Why

A tool configuration that half-loads is worse than one that does not load: an `exclude` that is silently empty means files the repository meant to skip are analysed, and a drift policy silently reset means a gate the repository relaxed is strict again. Reporting the parse failure and reverting everything to defaults is the honest state. Comments and trailing commas are accepted, so the file has a genuine syntax error at the quoted position.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
{ "exclude": ["**/Generated/**",] "canonical": { "drift": "warning" } }
```

Write:

```csharp
{ "exclude": ["**/Generated/**"], "canonical": { "drift": "warning" } }
```

## When it does not fire

Only `skala config check` surfaces it. The gate reader and the source-exclusion reader both fall back to defaults on the same broken file without repeating the report, so under `skala check` a broken `skala.jsonc` shows up as unexpected files in the run rather than as this id. It suppresses `SK9003` and `SK9012` for the same file, since neither runs over a document that did not parse.
